dct_description_sm: This was a multi-year project with the following over-arching goals: (1) to increase knowledge about climate change impacts on Aboriginal communities south of 60 latitude; (2) to increase knowledge about the risks climate change poses to Aboriginal communities south of 60 and how these risks are linked to other challenges and stressors; and (3) to assess the adaptive capacity of these communities and determine factors for why some Aboriginal communities may be at more risk than others. During the first year, the Centre for Indigenous Environmental Resources (CIER) aimed to initiate assessment of the adaptive capacity of Aboriginal communities, identify key exposures and sensitivities, develop the participatory research framework, identify potential case studies as well as potential vulnerability and/or risk assessment tools and assess their suitability for application in First Nations communities and settings.   The first year was also used to analyze research, identify information gaps and plan for upcoming years of the project. In its second year, the project maintained several of its objectives as well as initiated case study research with communities/organizations/regions and defined parameters for a tool to be developed in the following year of the project. That third and final year, the project consisted of creating an Aboriginal Climate Risk and Adaptive Capacity Assessment report and assessing the applicability of adaptation tools within communities.
